ai.literal: Self-control among immortals will lead; lack of self-control dense darkness having led will leave.
ai.translation: Self-control will elevate one to the realm of the immortals. A lack of self-control will plunge one into dense darkness.
ai.modern: அடக்கம் ஒருவனை தேவர்களுக்கு இணையாக உயர்த்தும். அடக்கமில்லாத தன்மை அவனை மீள முடியாத காரிருளில் தள்ளி அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the ultimate destinations of those who possess self-control and those who do not. The word அடக்கம் (self-control) is shown as an elevating force that places a person among the அமரர் (immortals), representing the highest state of being. Conversely, அடங்காமை (lack of restraint) leads one into ஆரிருள் (dense darkness), symbolizing a state of profound ignorance and suffering. The auxiliary verb விடும் emphasizes the absolute certainty and finality of this ruinous outcome.

ai.literal: Let one guard as wealth self-control; gain than that greater is not to life.
ai.translation: Guard self-control as a precious treasure. There is no greater wealth for a living being than that.
ai.modern: அடக்கத்தை ஒரு சிறந்த செல்வமாகப் போற்றிக் காக்க வேண்டும். ஒருயிருக்கு அதைவிடச் சிறந்த செல்வம் வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of self-control. It urges the reader to guard self-control as if it were the most precious material wealth. The word 'பொருள்' can mean meaning, reality, or wealth; here it specifically means wealth or treasure. Similarly, 'ஆக்கம்' can mean creation or prosperity, but here it means gain or wealth. The text states that for any living soul, there is no greater gain than mastering oneself, making self-control the ultimate treasure.

ai.literal: Firmness having known, greatness it will yield; knowledge having known, in the proper way to be restrained if achieved.
ai.translation: If one learns what is to be known and achieves self-restraint in the proper way, that firmness will be recognized and bring them greatness.
ai.modern: அறிய வேண்டியவற்றை அறிந்து, நல்வழியில் அடக்கத்துடன் நடந்தால், அந்த அடக்கத்தை உலகம் அறிந்து பெருமை தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the reward of disciplined self-restraint. It states that one must first acquire true knowledge and then apply it to restrain oneself in the righteous path. When a person achieves this, their steadfastness is recognized by the world, which in turn brings them immense greatness and respect.

ai.literal: From [his] state without swerving, of him who is self-controlled, the stature, even than a mountain, is greatly big.
ai.translation: The stature of one who remains self-controlled without swerving from his proper state is far greater than a mountain.
ai.modern: தன் நிலையிலிருந்து மாறாமல் அடக்கத்துடன் வாழ்பவனின் உயர்வு, மலையை விட மிகவும் பெரியதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the greatness of a self-controlled person to a mountain. The word 'nilai' refers to one's proper state or moral standing in life. When a person maintains this standing without swerving ('tiriyātu') and exercises self-restraint ('aṭaṅkiyāṉ'), their resulting stature ('tōṟṟam') becomes immense. The poet emphasizes this by stating that such a person's greatness is vastly larger ('māṇa peritu') even than a towering mountain.

ai.literal: To everyone good is humility; even among them, to the wealthy indeed wealth it has the nature of.
ai.translation: Humility is a good trait for everyone. Even among them, for the wealthy, it is like having an additional wealth.
ai.modern: அடக்கமாக இருத்தல் எல்லா மக்களுக்கும் நன்மையைத் தரும். அந்த மக்களுள்ளும், செல்வம் உடையவர்களுக்கு அந்த அடக்கமே மற்றொரு செல்வம் போன்ற சிறப்பினை உடையதாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet states that humility or self-restraint is a beneficial quality for all people. The word 'பணிதல்' means bowing down or being humble, which brings goodness ('நன்று') to everyone. However, the poet emphasizes that for those who are already wealthy ('செல்வர்'), this humility acts as an additional, crowning wealth ('செல்வம் தகைத்து'). While wealth can often make people arrogant, a wealthy person who remains humble possesses a virtue that outshines their material riches.

ai.literal: in one birth tortoise like five controlling if capable in seven births too protection it has
ai.translation: If a person can draw in their five senses like a tortoise in one lifetime, that self-control will protect them through seven lifetimes.
ai.modern: ஒரு பிறப்பில் ஆமை தன் ஐந்து உறுப்புகளையும் ஓட்டுக்குள் அடக்கிக்கொள்வது போல, ஒருவன் தன் ஐம்புலன்களையும் அடக்கியாள வல்லவனானால், அந்த அடக்கம் அவனுக்கு ஏழு பிறப்பிலும் பாதுகாப்பைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares a person controlling their senses to a tortoise drawing its four limbs and head into its shell. Here, the word 'ஐந்து' (five) specifically refers to the five senses, which must be withdrawn from external temptations. If one can master this self-control in a single lifetime, that discipline becomes an enduring armor. The text contrasts one birth with seven births to show that the spiritual protection ('ஏமாப்பு') gained from self-control extends far beyond the present life.

ai.literal: Whatever they guard not even if, tongue let them guard; if they guard not, they will grieve, word-slip having caught in.
ai.translation: Even if they guard nothing else, let them guard their tongue. If they do not, they will suffer, caught in a slip of words.
ai.modern: எவற்றைக் காக்கவில்லை என்றாலும் நாவையாவது காக்க வேண்டும். காக்கத் தவறினால் சொற்குற்றத்தில் சிக்கித் துன்பப்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of controlling one's speech. The word 'யா' means 'whatever', suggesting that even if a person fails to exercise restraint in other areas, they must at least control their tongue ('நா'). If they fail to do so ('காவாக்கால்'), they will inevitably make a slip of the tongue ('சொல் இழுக்கு'). Such careless words will cause them to suffer grief ('சோகாப்பர்') from the resulting consequences.

ai.literal: Even one / evil word / meaning's effect / if there is / goodness / will not become / having become / it will end up.
ai.translation: If a person's speech carries the harmful effect of even a single evil word, all their goodness will be ruined.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய பேச்சில் ஒரு தீய சொல்லின் பொருளால் விளையும் தீமை இருந்தாலும், அவருடைய நற்பண்புகள் எல்லாம் நல்லதாக இல்லாமல் அழிந்து போய்விடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the fragility of a good reputation in the face of careless speech. The phrase 'தீச்சொல் பொருட்பயன்' highlights that it is the harmful meaning and consequence of an evil word that causes the damage. The word 'ஒன்றானும்' stresses that even a single instance of such speech is sufficient to cause ruin. The concluding phrase 'நன்றாகா தாகி விடும்' illustrates a complete reversal, warning that any existing goodness will be nullified and turn into a lasting negative state.

ai.literal: By fire burnt wound inside will heal; will never heal by tongue burnt scar.
ai.translation: A wound burnt by fire will heal inside, but the scar burnt by a tongue will never heal.
ai.modern: தீயினால் சுட்ட புண் உடம்பின் உள்ளே காலப்போக்கில் ஆறிவிடும். ஆனால் ஒருவருடைய நாவினால் சுட்ட வடு ஒருபோதும் ஆறாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts physical injury with emotional harm to stress the importance of controlling one's speech. A physical burn from fire is described as a wound that will eventually heal inside. However, the damage caused by harsh words from the tongue is described as a scar, a permanent mark that will never heal. The precise choice of words highlights that while physical pain is temporary, the pain inflicted by words lasts forever.

ai.literal: Anger having guarded, having learned, restraining he who is capable, opportunity virtue will look for, in the way having entered.
ai.translation: Virtue will enter the path and wait for the opportune moment to approach the one who guards against anger, learns, and is capable of self-restraint.
ai.modern: சினத்தைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தி, கற்க வேண்டியவற்றைக் கற்று, அடக்கத்துடன் வாழ வல்லவனின் வழியில் நுழைந்து, அவனுக்கு நன்மை செய்ய அறம் தக்க நேரத்தை எதிர்பார்த்துக் காத்திருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet personifies virtue (அறம்) as an active force that seeks out the self-restrained person. The phrase 'கதம் காத்து' means guarding against anger, while 'கற்று அடங்கல் ஆற்றுவான்' refers to one who has learned and is capable of true self-restraint. For such a person, virtue itself will enter their path ('ஆற்றின் நுழைந்து') and wait for the right opportunity ('செவ்வி பார்க்கும்') to serve or bless them. The word 'செவ்வி' here means the proper time or opportunity, emphasizing that virtue eagerly awaits the chance to approach the disciplined individual.
